bounded_statement: The selected result applies Welch's two-sample t-test (a row-independent procedure) to all 60 measurement rows, even though the declared independent unit is reactor_id and each of the 10 reactors contributes 6 repeated sampling-day rows; the reported t = 14.26, df = 53.3, and p < 1e-12 therefore rest on an effective sample size of 60 rather than the 10 independent bioreactor units (5 per carbon source), inflating the degrees of freedom and overstating the strength of evidence. The direction of the effect (higher removal with glycerol) survives a reactor-level reanalysis, but the stated test statistics and p-value are not supported at the correct unit of analysis.

counterevidence_considered.description: The report transparently discloses the row-as-observation choice and accurately reports the clustered structure (10 bioreactors, 6 sampling occasions each), so the pooling is not concealed; however, disclosure does not make the row-independent t-test valid for repeated-unit data.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: explicit statement that each sampling-day measurement was entered as one observation

evidence.description: The input data show strong within-reactor clustering: each reactor's six repeated values span only about 0.1 mg N/L/h (e.g., R01 ranges 3.04-3.15), while reactor means within a group differ by up to ~0.65 (e.g., R03 ~2.95 vs R04 ~3.60), so rows from the same reactor are highly correlated and not exchangeable with rows from other reactors.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify the pseudoreplication claim in three ways. (1) Checked whether reactor_id might actually vary within the treatment comparison in a way that makes rows independent: the CSV confirms each reactor keeps one carbon source for all six rows, so rows are strict repeated measures of one unit. (2) Checked whether the workflow performs any per-reactor aggregation or clustering adjustment before testing: it only counts reactors (per_reactor, reactors sets) for reporting, while the t-test consumes the raw 30-vs-30 row-level lists, and the reported df = 53.3 matches pooled-row Welch degrees of freedom (a unit-level analysis could give at most df = 8). (3) Checked whether the issue is immaterial by recomputing at the unit level: a 5-vs-5 Welch t-test on reactor means gives approximately t = 4.8, df = 8, p ~ 0.001 — still significant, so the conclusion's direction survives, but the selected result's t = 14.26, df = 53.3, and p < 1e-12 are artifacts of entering each independent unit six times. The falsification attempts failed to overturn the issue: the procedure demonstrably received repeated entries per independent unit.

root_cause: The workflow pools every CSV row directly into stats.ttest_ind by carbon_source without aggregating repeated measurements per reactor_id or using a model that accounts for within-reactor correlation, so each independent unit (bioreactor) is entered six times into a procedure that assumes each entry is an independent observation.
